answer:
**Credit allocation and causal incrementality are different questions.** A customer may see an ad immediately before purchasing because they were already searching for that product. Giving the last ad credit describes a path; it does not establish that the ad caused the purchase. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874)

Shapley attribution distributes credit according to a chosen value function over channel combinations. Markov removal methods assess changes in a fitted path model when a channel is removed. Both can be useful summaries while inheriting selection and model assumptions.

**An experiment changes exposure deliberately.** A randomized holdout or suitable geo-lift design compares outcomes under a defined intervention, subject to spillover and adequate power. Such evidence can calibrate observational attribution or broader marketing models.

Specify attribution windows, identity matching, unobserved channels, and the intervention being evaluated. Credit summing to 100% is an accounting property, not proof that advertising caused every conversion. Nor does the current credit split necessarily optimize the next budget: marginal returns can differ from historical average associations. Use attribution for its descriptive role and causal evidence for incremental decisions.

**Technical details and references.**

Shapley attribution distributes credit across observed channel combinations according to a chosen value function; Markov removal effects measure changes in a fitted path model when a channel is removed. Both can describe associations while mistaking intent-driven exposure for causal influence. [1](https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874)

A search ad may appear just before purchase because the user already intended to buy. Geo-lift or other randomized holdouts estimate incremental outcomes under a defined intervention, subject to spillover and power constraints. Use experiments to calibrate observational attribution/MMM where possible.

Keep attribution windows, identity resolution, missing channels, and privacy constraints explicit. Allocated credit summing to 100% does not prove that 100% of conversions were caused by advertising or that the same allocation optimizes the next budget.
